captured_content: IMF reports Nigeria end-period CPI inflation of 21.3% in 2022 and 28.9% in 2023, and describes inflation as driven mainly by food-price inflation and loose financial conditions in early 2024; it also records sharp naira depreciation after the June 2023 FX-window unification and notes risks from food, oil and global-price shocks.

IMF 2026 analysis describes Nigeria's inflation as historically driven by food prices, supply-side shocks, deficit financing and episodes of pronounced exchange-rate depreciation, including after the 2023 FX-window unification.
DMO records Anambra domestic debt at N6,403.32 million as at 31 December 2011.
DMO records Anambra total domestic debt at N14,299.99 million as at 31 December 2012.
DMO's revised 2013 state debt table records Anambra domestic debt at N3,025,797,046.67 as at December 2013.

BPE describes the NCP/BPE structure as driving privatisation, sector reforms and liberalisation; it says the NCP established a Telecommunications Sector Reform Implementation Committee in 2000 and that BPE collaborated with ministries, the National Assembly, labour and the private sector.
BPE's NITEL record states that GSM licences were issued in February 2001, including licences to MTN, V-Mobile and NITEL, and describes regulatory and licensing arrangements involving the NCC.
An archived Daily Trust page from April 2001 identifies Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as NCP Chairman in coverage of NCP activities.
